principles: An OPEN epoch binds the selected candidate universe, not incidental ranking order or reroute freshness metadata.
A persisted artifact is untrusted runtime input even when TypeScript declares its shape; invalid input must produce a named fail-closed lifecycle result.
The regression must exercise real git changedPaths and the real handler invalidation path.
Canonical barrier narrowing must not alter the independently verified full artifactDigest tamper contract.
drivers: Prevent an unrelated commit from invalidating an otherwise unchanged REVIEW epoch.
Retain invalidation for a changed selected path or content hash.
Make the B-3f3d F-108 failure reproducible without destructive stash operations.
Expose malformed or tampered persisted artifacts as a stable typed epoch-invalidation reason.

options.name: Semantic sorted barrier projection plus strict artifact guard
pros: Makes order irrelevant while retaining selected path and content-hash identity.
Leaves artifactDigest tamper verification unchanged and explicitly tested.
Allows a dedicated typed invalid-artifact blocker through the actual handler path.
cons: Requires a scope-shape addition, blocker union/document update, and regression coverage in two smoke suites.

options.name: Stabilize the router output order only
cons: Does not protect the barrier from alternate valid producers or future ordering changes.
Does not address malformed persisted candidates.

options.name: Continue comparing full artifactDigest
cons: Preserves the confirmed freshness false positive and fails the user outcome.

chosen: Semantic sorted barrier projection plus strict artifact guard
rationale: The barrier must compare a canonical set of selected path/content pairs. A runtime type guard prevents malformed JSON from escaping into map() and lets persistInvalidationIfDrifted report the typed OPEN_REVIEW_INVENTORY_INVALID_CANDIDATE_ARTIFACT result. Full artifact identity stays independently verified and is negatively tested after the comparator narrows. The decision record is updated when the historical known-incomplete statement is conclusively closed.

preMortem.scenario: Sorting masks a genuine candidate change.
preMortem.trigger: A changed selected path or content hash produces the same barrier digest.
preMortem.consequence: An OPEN epoch would mix review evidence from different candidate universes.
preMortem.mitigation: Test positive invariance only for reordered equal path/content pairs and a negative test for changed path/content.

preMortem.scenario: The malformed artifact is silently treated as absent.
preMortem.trigger: A non-array candidates artifact omits the scope digest without recording invalidity.
preMortem.consequence: Operators cannot distinguish a bad artifact from no routing artifact.
preMortem.mitigation: Carry explicit invalid-artifact state into persistInvalidationIfDrifted, add the blocker to the closed type union, and assert its rendered text.

preMortem.scenario: The new regression never populates changedPaths.
preMortem.trigger: Fixture remains on main or commits before creating the story branch.
preMortem.consequence: The false-green test passes without exercising the original leak.
preMortem.mitigation: Assert git diff main...HEAD is nonempty before rerouting and assert State: OPEN afterwards.

preMortem.scenario: Canonicalization bypasses the old tamper detector.
preMortem.trigger: A modified artifact no longer needs its artifactDigest to verify.
preMortem.consequence: Persisted routing data could silently bypass integrity validation.
preMortem.mitigation: Retain full artifactDigest verification and run a mutation-negative candidate-routing smoke.
